originality.rationale: For each admissible symmetric design, the complete powered-distance zero-sum spectrum is established and the sharp phase boundary is derived. The projective-plane/complement comparison changes both the leading exponent scale and the critical Hilbert dimension. The inspected primary literature treats unpowered distance kernels, general QE criteria, join graphs, or Laplacian group inverses, rather than these fractional thresholds and the two competing zero-mode mechanisms. The prior crown-graph special family r=1 is excluded. This is a best-knowledge assessment, not proof of global historical novelty.
residual_risks: A generalized distance-regular-graph or association-scheme formula for every real distance power may imply this specialization without the same wording; no exhaustive search of all older monographs was possible.
The 2018 QE primary PDF was only materially inspected in its relevant early sections, not line-by-line throughout; negative coverage is not inferred from a mere download.
Literature search cannot establish historical uniqueness; independent priority review remains necessary.
The existence of admissible nontrivial symmetric designs with simultaneous spectral/global zero modes is unresolved and not claimed.

value.rationale: A complete all-admissible-parameter classification for a natural family of diameter-three design graphs is a substantive quantitative Hilbert-embedding invariant. It separates two genuinely different obstruction mechanisms, determines their complete endpoint equality dimensions, and proves a sharp incidence-versus-nonincidence phase switch with different asymptotic scales q^(-1/2) and q^(-2). It covers nonisomorphic designs with identical parameters, including arbitrary finite projective planes, and expressly excludes the known crown r=1 family; no unmotivated finite slice or mere numerical table is needed.
